header: Francesca’s customers, girls aged 11 to 15, were outgrowing the brand. At Phenomenon, we reimagined it as a stylish older sister, with a new look and a new way to shop online. I was the visual and product designer.

layout.title: Outgrowing the brand
text: Francesca’s was built for younger girls. But its customers had grown more style-aware and were drifting toward brands like Madewell and Asos. A new look alone wouldn’t fix that. The brand needed a new personality, and the site needed to deliver it at every step of shopping, without alienating parents.

layout.title: Stylish, not intimidating
text: I designed a brand direction that balanced trend-forward style with approachability. It had a brighter palette, editorial photography, and a more confident tone. It tested well across audiences.

layout.title: Shopping like a magazine
text: Working with Phenomenon’s strategists, I carried the brand into the site by taking cues from fashion magazines. I designed an editorial layer that suggested product pairings instead of pushing promotions, so shopping felt like advice from an older sister, not a sales pitch.
In user testing, the editorial layer was one of the favorite parts of the new site. I also redesigned the checkout, and we tested several flows with users to find the simplest path to purchase.

layout.title: Result
text: The redesign never launched after the client’s priorities shifted, but the direction held up where it counted. It tested well with both girls and parents.
